issue_title: Vapor: comments inside <TransitionGroup> are dropped by SSR (by design, #11961) but kept by the vapor client, desynchronizing hydration
issue_body:
### Vue version 3.6.0-rc.6 ### Link to minimal reproduction https://github.com/denismrte/vapor-transitiongroup-comment-hydration ### Steps to reproduce Steps to reproduce pnpm install pnpm verify verify.mjs server-renders four variants of one template, hydrates each in headless Chromium and prints what each did. It exits 0 when the bug signature is present, 1 when it is absent, 2 on a harness failure. The failing component, src/Fail.vue, is a vapor SFC with a single comment as a direct child of a . The button only proves the app is live. Server: renderToString(createSSRApp(App)). Client: createVaporSSRApp(App).mount('#app'). ### What is expected? Hydration adopts the server tree unchanged, as it already does for the same template compiled as a vdom component, and as it does for the same vapor template with the comment removed ### What is actually happening?

The vapor client walks one node out of step and inserts a duplicate item for every comment it cannot find in the server HTML.

case | server 
  • | after hydration | mismatch reported -- | -- | -- | -- vapor, one comment inside  | ["a","b","c"] | ["a","a","b","c"] | yes vapor, two comments in that position | ["a","b","c"] | ["a","b","a","b","c"] | yes vapor, same template without the comment | ["a","b","c"] | ["a","b","c"] | no vdom, comment inside  | ["a","b","c"] | ["a","b","c"] | no

    Server HTML (the comment is absent, which is correct — see below):

    <!--[--><button id="bump">bump</button><p id="clicks">0</p><ul><!--[--><li>a</li><li>b</li><li>c</li><!--]--></ul><!--]-->

    DOM after hydration:

    <!--[--><button id="bump">bump</button><p id="clicks">0</p><ul><!--[--><li>a</li><li>a</li><li>b</li><li>c</li><!--]--><!--transition-group--></ul><!--]-->

    Browser output:

    [Vue warn]: Hydration node mismatch:
- rendered on server: li
- expected on client: <!-- a comment as a direct child of the transition group -->
  at <VaporTransitionGroup appear=false persisted=false onBeforeEnter=undefined  ... >
  at <Fail >
Hydration completed but contains mismatches.
[Vue warn]: Hydration text mismatch in li
  - rendered on server: "b"
  - expected on client: "a"
[Vue warn]: Hydration text mismatch in li
  - rendered on server: "c"
  - expected on client: "b"
[Vue warn]: Hydration node mismatch:
- rendered on server: #comment
- expected on client: <li>
[Vue warn]: <transition-group> children must be keyed

    Each further comment shifts the cursor one node more and duplicates one more item — the two case in the reproduction is that same template with a second comment, and it duplicates two.

    The page stays interactive in every arm: hydration completes, reports the mismatch and leaves a tree that no longer matches the server's.

    ### System Info ```shell System: OS: macOS 26.4.1 CPU: arm64 Binaries: Node: 24.19.0 pnpm: 11.22.0 Browsers: Chrome: 152.0.7977.64 npmPackages: vue: 3.6.0-rc.6 vite: 8.2.2 @vitejs/plugin-vue: 6.0.8 ``` ### Any additional comments? The server side is behaving as designed. ssrProcessTransitionGroup passes disableComment: true into processChildren, with this reason in the source: TransitionGroup filters out comment children at runtime and thus doesn't expect comments to be present during hydration. That is the fix for #11958, landed as #11961 (fix(ssr): don't render comments in TransitionGroup), and it also suppresses the placeholder a falsy v-if would otherwise emit there (#6715). So the omission is deliberate and the vdom client agrees with it. What is missing is the vapor half of that contract: the vapor compiler or the vapor TransitionGroup hydration path still expects the comment nodes SSR is designed never to write. Either the vapor compiler should drop comment children of a the way the vdom runtime filters them, or vapor hydration should skip them the way disableComment assumes. A vapor app whose only symptom is a stray duplicated row is easy to misread as a keying problem, so the failure hides well.
